chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who was killed and had young and adult children. I asked: What is your view if the adult children forgive? He said: He would not be killed, and the forgiveness of the adult children is valid regarding their shares. So when the young ones grow up, it is for them to claim their shares from the blood money.
ai.seo_question: How does the forgiveness of adult children affect the retaliation for a father's murder when minor children are also heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia jurisprudential principle that the forgiveness of adult heirs in qisas (retaliation) is binding for their specific shares, thereby preventing the killer's execution even if minors later claim their portion. It highlights the distinction between the right to kill (qisas) and the right to compensation (diyah), a key topic in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the nature of inheritance rights in blood money. The ruling ensures that the killer is not executed for the minors' share, preserving the integrity of the adult heirs' initial decision.
